title: CSV parser that handles quotes and line breaks
when: JavaScript code must read CSV text (from a file input, a fetch or Node) where fields can hold commas, quotes or line breaks.
inputs: whether the first row is a header
prompt:
Goal: A small state machine parser following RFC 4180 that returns rows or objects and reports malformed lines by number.
Steps:
1. Strip a leading BOM (\uFEFF) and walk the text character by character with states: field start, unquoted, quoted, quote seen inside quotes.
2. Inside quotes, "" is one literal quote and commas or line breaks are data; a quote closes the field only before a delimiter, a line end or the end.
3. End rows on \n, \r\n or \r outside quotes; drop empty trailing lines.
4. Unknown delimiter: count , ; and tab outside quotes on the first line and take the most frequent.
5. Header mode: trim header names, make duplicates unique (name, name_2), keep every value as a string.
6. Collect problems (unclosed quote, wrong column count) as { line, message } instead of throwing; convert types later, per column.
Quality bar:
- Round trip with the matching writer keeps data identical.
- 50 thousand rows parse without freezing; bigger files go to a worker.
- Error lines refer to the original file.
Pitfalls:
- split("\n") then split(","), which breaks on quoted commas and line breaks.
- Trimming values that carry meaningful spaces.
- Guessing numbers from strings like 007 or 1,5.
Verify:
- [ ] Tests cover quoted commas, doubled quotes, CRLF and a line break inside quotes.
- [ ] BOM removed.
- [ ] Column count problems reported with line numbers.
- [ ] No eval or Function.
Output: js/csv.js exporting parseCSV(text, { delimiter, header }) and a test file with the tricky cases.

examples.input: meu import de csv quebra quando o endereço tem vírgula
examples.output: parseCSV state machine honoring "Rua A, 10" quoted fields, doubled quotes and CRLF, with tests
